Suzuki-ya chisel page: nomi divided first by use into striking chisels (oire-nomi bench, chu-tataki-nomi, atsu-nomi, tateguya mortise) and push or paring chisels (usu-nomi, shinogi-nomi, tsuki-nomi, yama-ari-nomi dovetail); then by named maker (Ohuchi, Takamichi, Fujikawa Yasaku)

Japan House London essay: 1943 Ota Ward survey found 179 tool types needed for a full-quality building (72 for cheaper build), 1985 survey only 20 used often; groups axes (ono), marking (sumi-kake, kebiki), saws (nokogiri), planes (kanna, awase-kanna), hammers (genno: ryoguchi, funate, kataguchi), chisels (striking versus paring)

EU Combined Nomenclature heading 8467 hand-held power tools: split by energy (pneumatic, self-contained electric motor, other motor) then by action (drills, saws including chainsaws and circular saws, grinders and sanders including angle grinders and belt sanders, planers, hedge trimmers), parts separate

HS chapter 82 headings by action: 8201 agricultural hand tools, 8202 saws, 8203 files/pliers/shears/punches, 8204 spanners and wrenches, 8205 other hand tools (vices, clamps, anvils), 8206 sets, 8207 interchangeable tools, 8208 machine knives; powered hand tools go to 8467, so customs separates hand from powered tools and keeps accessories separate

Wikipedia Antique tool: collectors organise by maker (Stanley, Disston, Norris, Miller's Falls), type (hammers, braces, axes, saws, patented and transitional planes), period, place, occupation (cooper, machinist, watchmaker), and type study of one model (Stanley #6 jointer, Norris A5 smoother); lists collector associations (Mid-West Tool Collectors Association, Early American Industries Association, Tools and Trades History Society, Hand Tool Preservation Association of Australia)

Wikipedia Hand tool: general categories attributed to the American Industrial Hygiene Association are wrenches, pliers, cutters, striking tools, struck or hammered tools, screwdrivers, vises, clamps, snips, saws, drills, knives; portable power tools excluded; division is by mechanical action

Highland Woodworking plane guide: planes grouped by role and length into smoothers (Stanley 1 to 4-1/2), jack planes (5, 5-1/2, 6) and jointers (6, 7, 8) using the Stanley numbering; buyers choose between refurbished antique Stanley and premium modern makers such as Lie-Nielsen (flat out of the box)
